overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the executive session purpose and vote allegations, declined to review the notice allegation as already decided in OML 2024-167, and treated the misleading-statement claim as not a violation.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly met in executive session for an improper purpose on Nov 13 and Dec 4, 2023, discussing the Superintendent's contract renewal.
allegations.key_passage: We conclude that the Committee properly met in executive session in November and December and thus did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly voted in the Dec 4, 2023 executive session not to renew the Superintendent's contract, which must be done in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Committee took a vote in executive session, we find that the Committee was simply deciding on a course of action with respect to the future employment of the Superintendent and was not ratifying or executing a contract.

allegations.summary: Jan 8, 2024 meeting notice allegedly omitted the Superintendent nonrenewal topic that the Chair announced at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review the third allegation because we have already decided the issue in a previous determination.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly misled the public by announcing at the Jan 8, 2024 meeting that an agreement had been reached with the Superintendent.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, even if true, this allegation would not be a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
